//: Input to tools/fetch-media.py. Licensing is the whole problem with this subject
and it is worth writing down why each of these is safe, because 1940 is NOT a
year where you can assume anything is public domain.
Three safe families are used here, and nothing else:
1. UK Crown copyright photographs taken before 1957. Crown copyright in a
photograph expired 50 years after creation, so Royal Navy and War Office
official pictures from 1940 are genuinely out of copyright. These are the
Imperial War Museum plates: A21, A39, A24, A42, HU91803, HU93727, N159,
2. Arkiv i Nordland's Flickr Commons collection, released CC BY-SA 2.0.
Commercially usable with credit, which fetch-media.py records.
3. Bundesarchiv, CC BY-SA 3.0 de. Also commercially usable with credit.
NOTE the Bundesarchiv captions are the ORIGINAL German wartime captions
and are propaganda; the titles below are ours, not theirs.
Deliberately NOT used: anything the Imperial War Museum offers only under its
own non-commercial licence, anything on Commons where a modern uploader has
claimed CC on an obviously old photograph they did not take, and Polish
wartime material where the PD claim rests on an unnamed author. Where a
picture had to be dropped for that reason the map carries the beat instead.
There is one honest gap. There is no well-licensed photograph of Norwegian
soldiers on the Narvik front at a size that stands up to a full-screen plate:
the ones on Commons are 400-600 px. The 6th Division therefore appears on the
map and in the portraits rather than in a picture of its own, which is a
licensing outcome and not an editorial judgement.
